AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  JULY 19, 2022
UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF
ASSEMBLY BILL 361, WHICH ALLOWS COUNCIL MEMBERS TO PARTICIPATE FROM A REMOTE
LOCATION WITHOUT LISTING A PHYSICAL LOCATION. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS DURING A MEETING:
YOU MAY ATTEND THE MEETING, SEND AN EMAIL TO: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, OR JOIN THE
ZOOM MEETING BY CALLING: (669) 900-6833 OR USING THE ZOOM APP WITH THE FOLLOWING LINK:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/7095732685; MEETING ID: 709 573 2685. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED
THROUGH ZOOM, FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR CHARTER CHANNEL 3, OR ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT:
https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-agendas-393.
  5:15 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Rick Ramirez, Mayor
  Ana Valencia, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember
  Jennifer Perez, Councilmember
  Margarita L. Rios, Councilmember
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.
 CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ramirez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – EXISTING LITIGATION PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT
  CODE SECTION 54956.9(d)(1) - City of Long Beach, et al. v. Monsanto Company, et al., United States
  District Court, Central District of California – Western Division, Case No.: 2:16-cv-03493-FMO-AS.

  II.  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6; CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR.
  Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager regarding negotiations with the
  Norwalk Association of Management Employees.

  III.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Property: Assessor Property Numbers 8056-015-014 and 8056-025-020; Negotiating
  Parties: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager, on behalf of the City and Primestor Development Inc.; Under
  Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.

  IV.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - ANTICIPATED  LITIGATION  PURSUANT  TO
  GOVERNMENT CODE ?54956.9(d)(2) in one case.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ramirez

INVOCATION
  Pastor Nathan Butterfield
  Community Chapel World Outreach

FLAG SALUTE
  Adrienne Romero
  Dolland Elementary

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

  I.  City Council to recognize the winners of the City’s “Say No to Illegal Fireworks” Art competition.

  II.  City Council to recognize July as Parks and Recreation month in the City of Norwalk.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  COVID-19 Update.
   2.  July 4th Enforcement Update.

  3.  Department Highlights – Community Development.

  4.  Bi-Weekly Review.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meetings of June
  28, and July 5, 2022. 825-04

  Minutes

  2.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period June 26, 2022 – July 9,
  2022, in the total amount of $1,086,592.89. 630

  Report

  3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period June
  28 through July 11, 2022 in the total amount of $2,921,908.03. 640

  Warrant Register

  4.  CLAIMS AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claim filed by Claudia
  Velasco. 830-22

  Report

  5.  PLANNING COMMISSION SYNOPSIS – July 13, 2022 - No action is required unless the City Council
  elects to review the decision of the Planning Commission on those items where the Commission’s
  action was final. 320

  Report

  6.  ASSEMBLY BILL 361 FINDINGS - Staff recommends City Council make the following findings:

  a.  City Council has reconsidered the circumstances of the state of emergency.

  b.  Both of the following circumstances exist (i) The state of emergency continues to directly impact
  the ability of the members to meet safely in person and (ii) City Council continues to impose or
  recommend measures to promote social distancing including remote or hybrid meeting
  participation. 825

  Report

  7.  RESOLUTION NO. 22-41 - APPROVING AMENDMENT NO. 5 FOR THE SUPPORTIVE SERVICES
  PROGRAM FOR FISCAL YEAR 2022/23 - Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No.22-41,
  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK APPROVING AMENDMENT
  NO. 5 TO THE AGREEMENT FOR THE SUPPORTIVE SERVICES PROGRAM WITH THE LOS
  ANGELES WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, AGING AND COMMUNITY SERVICES FOR FISCAL
  YEAR 2022/23 AND AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER TO EXECUTE THE AMENDMENT, in the
  amount of $59,000, from July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023. 425-02-05

  Report

  8.  RESOLUTION NO. 22-42 – FISCAL YEAR 2022/23 TRANSPORTATION DEVELOPMENT ACT
  ARTICLE 4 AND STATE TRANSIT ASSISTANCE ARTICLE 6.5 FUND ALLOCATIONS - Staff
  recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-42, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF
  THE CITY OF NORWALK ADOPTING THE USE OF TRANSPORTATION DEVELOPMENT ACT
  ARTICLE 4 AND STATE TRANSIT ASSISTANCE ARTICLE 6.5 FUNDS FOR FISCAL YEAR 2022/23.
   1105-02

  Report

  9.  PROJECT NO. 7857 – AWARD OF CONTRACT – CONSTRUCTION FOR ENVIRONMENTAL
  ENHANCEMENT & MITIGATION PROGRAM GRANT FUNDED MEDIAN TURF REPLACEMENT ON
  IMPERIAL HIGHWAY, ROSECRANS AVENUE, AND FIRESTONE BOULEVARD - Staff recommends
  City Council award a contract to KASA Construction, Inc. of Chino, California for Project No. 7857 –
  EEMP Grant Funded Median Turf Replacement on Imperial Highway, Rosecrans Avenue, and
  Firestone Boulevard construction in the amount of $223,706; and authorize the City Manager to
  execute the contract and any amendments provided there is funding in the budget and it is within the
  City Manager’s signing authority, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 1004-
  05-7857

  Report

  10. AUTHORIZE SIGNATURE AUTHORITY FOR FUNCTIONAL REPLACEMENT AREA IN LIEU OF
  PAYMENT OF COMPENSATION FOR PARK LAND AND NORWALK NATURE CENTER ON
  PORTIONS OF NORWALK PARK - Staff recommends City Council authorize the City Manager to
  execute any agreements, amendments, and escrow documents for the functional replacement area in
  lieu of payment of compensation for park land and Norwalk Park Nature Center on portions of Norwalk
  Park, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 920-03-10

  Report

  11. CORONAVIRUS PANDEMIC – JULY EMERGENCY OPERATIONS CENTER UPDATE – Receive and
  file. 710-07

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  12. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

PUBLIC HEARING

  13. DELINQUENT REFUSE COLLECTION ACCOUNTS - Staff recommends City Council approve the lien
  lists for the delinquent accounts that are not paid by July 31, 2022, and authorize staff to forward a final
  list to the Los Angeles County Tax Assessor. 626-02

  Report

RESOLUTION

  14. RESOLUTION NO. 22-43 - APPROVING THE MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN
  THE CITY OF NORWALK AND THE NORWALK ASSOCIATION OF EXECUTIVE MANAGEMENT
  AND MID-MANAGEMENT EMPLOYEES FROM JULY 1, 2022 THROUGH JUNE 30, 2025 AND
  RESOLUTION NO. 22-44 - APPROVING A REVISED SALARY SCHEDULE FOR FISCAL YEAR
  2022/23 – Staff recommends City Council adopt:

  a.  Resolution No. 22-43, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  APPROVING THE MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN THE CITY OF NORWALK
  AND THE NORWALK ASSOCIATION OF MANAGEMENT EMPLOYEES; and

  b.  Resolution No. 22-44, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  AMENDING THE SALARY SCHEDULE FOR FISCAL YEAR 2022/23 FOR THE GENERAL,
  HOURLY, AND EXECUTIVE MANAGEMENT AND MID-MANAGEMENT EMPLOYEES. 135-17

  Report

REPORTS
   15. NEIGHBORHOOD REHABILITATION PROGRAM FOR THE ONE-WAYS - Staff recommends City
  Council approve the One-Ways Revitalization Program. 1410-01

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated July 15, 2022.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
